provenance: Deliberately wrong fixture for `make checkpoint-negatives` (#25). A copy of post-opera-v1's payload with one byte changed: the slot-3 element-codex row (SRAM 0x293D, SNES $31693D, ULTROS2) flipped 0x00 -> 0x01, with the sha256 recomputed so it re-validates and cold-boots. It models a checkpoint whose content drifted from its contract, and post-opera-v1's entry contract must fail naming that one field. It is not produced by the game's save routine, which is the point; no generate rule may name it. Rebuilt 2026-08-11 from the re-cut post-opera-v1: the previous copy predated e65af20, differed from it in 98 bytes, and perturbed a row the re-cut contract no longer expected, so the negative fired on the class-codex row while the script grepped for the element-codex one.  Rebuilt again 2026-10-06 from the current post-opera-v1 payload (sha256 670f3cd09ecf2b03345cee0f8144f963f55bf65fa75e9ad6f1a47aa5ba7ce05f), the same one byte flipped: the 2026-08-11 copy predated #305 (362 bytes adrift, TERRA's and CELES's Antdot learned, #335).
